name: Silver Fizz

instructions.primary_message: In a cocktail shaker, dissolve the sugar in the lemon juice; add the gin and egg white and shake, without ice, for about 10 seconds to give the egg white some froth. Add ice to the shaker and shake vigorously for a good 10 seconds, to work up the foam. Strain into a chilled Collins glass and top with about 2 ounces of club soda. If you're in the mood for it, dash some bitters atop the foam.

schema_metadata.keywords: cocktails, egg whites, eggs, gin, lemon juice, raw eggs

description: Fizzes were introduced as morning drinks in the 19th century, eye-opening hangover remedies with the added benefit of a bit of egg white to help it all go down. It's simply a Tom Collins chilled and shaken with egg white, served without ice (fizzes are designed to be consumed fairly quickly, not lingered over for a half-hour).
notes: Optional or for serving: bitters, optional
author: Paul Clarke
